item: absent field vs zero values vs empty string
dispositionCell: **HELD**: the two cell states a device tells apart: no element (zero values) and an empty element (an empty string, or a field absent from the row, which HQ writes the same way, `fixturegenerators.py::to_xml`). Project data keeps an absent field, an empty list and an empty string apart (`lib/lookup/rowContent.ts`), the reading takes a zero-occurrence field from its row detail, the device fixture writes each as HQ's restore does, and the workbook refuses a row HQ's reader would not reconstruct. The `hq-lookup-data` base holds all three in one field, and its device fixture matches HQ's restore element for element (`proof/hq/test_lookup_fixtures.py`); Core compares a missing element and an empty one alike, so its choice list filtered on the empty value offers all three rows

item: table or row count beyond Nova's caps (5,000 rows, 250 columns, 64 KiB cell, 256 KiB row, 8 MiB table)
dispositionCell: **HELD-NEW**: these Nova limits apply to one inline request or stored value. Larger complete tables and cells can be read in pages. The downloadable app budgets its unindexed embedded fixtures across inline and streamed tables at 10,000 rows, 100,000 cells and 16 MiB of exact fixture XML. CommCare HQ accepts at most 500,000 rows per workbook including both sheet headers and the types-sheet declarations, so one table fits up to 499,997 data rows. Nova can split workbooks between complete tables. Direct JSON can send complete global unindexed paged tables whose values the workbook cannot preserve. It verifies exact row bodies before writes, saves progress at settled operations and limits one publish to 10,000 paged JSON rows and 16 MiB of request bodies. The authenticated manual installer carries the same bounded JSON data and resumes through the same verified row journal before the separate app import. CommCare worker storage caps a value at 65,535 modified UTF-8 bytes. Larger tables beyond both carriers remain held
